requirements.requirement: An opsbot account exists on node1 and a corresponding opsbot identity exists on node2 for remote command execution.
requirements.summary: Direct checks show locked-password opsbot accounts on both nodes, including after each reboot.

requirements.requirement: opsbot on node1 can use an SSH key to run commands as opsbot on node2.
requirements.summary: Successful SSH sessions from node1 executed identity, hostname, and command probes as UID 1000 opsbot on node2. The client public key and node2 authorized key have the same fingerprint, and access continued after both reboots.

requirements.requirement: SSH authentication for opsbot requires public-key authentication on both systems.
requirements.summary: Effective sshd configuration on both nodes requires publickey and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. Password-only connection attempts to each node were rejected with publickey as the only offered method, including in final post-reboot checks.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. opsbot exists with locked passwords, node1 has a protected ED25519 client key whose fingerprint matches node2's authorized key, node1 successfully runs commands as opsbot on node2, and effective SSH policy enforces public-key-only authentication for opsbot on both systems. Both mandatory node restarts were directly observed and followed by full recovery.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots independently confirm reboot identities and general system health but do not inventory accounts or SSH configuration; those outcomes rely on direct executor command observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace. Account, key, sshd-policy, and known-host changes directly implement the task. Host-key generation and creation of /run/sshd were necessary prerequisites after diagnostics showed missing host keys/runtime state; service operations enabled and validated SSH. Temporary negative-test files were removed. Both nodes finished with no failed services, healthy package state, and only the expected SSH exposure. The restart protocol was complete on both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH policy, key data, and functional access.
